purpose: Follow up the exact Hinabaan River fish-source discovery lead. The search records a bounded retrieval result, not fish absence.
queries: Guinayangan Quezon freshwater fish survey river Hinabaan
"Hinabaan River" biodiversity OR ichthyofauna OR fishes
searchMethod: Public search-engine discovery on 2026-11-01 using exact river/falls names, fish/ichthyofauna terms, municipality-level freshwater survey terms, and domain-restricted UPLB, SEAFDEC, and BMB repository searches. This is not an exhaustive literature or agency-archive search.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Guinayangan Water District. Annual Report for Calendar Year 2024, Annex J: List of Water Sources.
sourcesReviewed.reviewedLocation: Annex J, printed page 38; report text lines 2562-2582
sourcesReviewed.result: Lists Hinabaan River under surface-water sources at Brgy. Balinarin/Hinabaan with the operational status label Flowing.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Water-supply source and locality context only. The report gives no fish taxa or fish-survey methods; Flowing is not a water-quality, ecological-flow, or safety finding.

sourcesReviewed.citation: DENR CALABARZON / CENRO Calauag. DENR Calauag monitors 2026 Asian Waterbird Populations Across Quezon Province's Wetlands.
sourcesReviewed.result: Describes a January 2026 Asian Waterbird Census and names the Hinabaan barangay context alongside Ragay Gulf and De Guzman Fishpond; the stated observations concern waterbirds.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Not fish evidence and not a crosswalk to Hinabaan River. Direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403 in the prior review; current search-indexed content was checked.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Municipality of Guinayangan. Natures Wonder / Hinabaan Falls.
sourcesReviewed.result: The municipal tourism page names Hinabaan Falls in Barangay Hinabaan, Guinayangan.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Falls/locality tourism context only. The page provides no fish survey, taxon list, station, coordinates, or crosswalk showing the falls are the same feature as the water-district's Hinabaan River.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Bangwit research review of fish-survey discovery for eight Guinayangan freshwater leads, including Hinabaan River.
sourcesReviewed.result: The prior bounded CoL XR Actinopterygii GBIF screen recorded zero results for the supplied Hinabaan River/Hinabaan locality and waterBody strings, plus municipality text.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Retained as a bounded indexed-text search gap only; no fish-absence inference. No new GBIF request was made in this follow-up.

limitations: Search-engine and repository-index results are discovery aids, not an exhaustive search of theses, local reports, unpublished surveys, or collection databases.
The DENR source describes a waterbird census and nearby site context, not a fish survey or a river-specific observation.
The municipal tourism page identifies Hinabaan Falls but does not establish that the falls and source-named Hinabaan River are one feature.
The 2024 water-district report describes a supply-source listing only and provides no fish, water-quality, geometry, or access evidence.
The earlier GBIF zero-result text screen is not evidence of fish absence, and no new API screen or occurrence record was reviewed here.
No fish taxa, coordinates, geometry, salinity, current presence, fishing access, legality, safety, catchability, diet, or public-app rows were established.
nextAction: Continue the remaining Guinayangan freshwater leads independently. Prioritize the Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape and its named tributaries for primary fish-monitoring outputs; keep the separately named Hinabaan River and Viñas River unmerged until an authoritative feature crosswalk is found.
